newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on harvest pressure.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on harvest pressure.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on harvest pressure with commercial selling tied to hedge selling again a feature in new crop July, traders said.
A six-month low was notched in new crop July as that month touched $3.32-1/4 per bushel, the lowest level since $3.30 was traded on December 11.

The wheat market remained pressured by active harvesting and reports of better-than-expected yields. Hard red winter wheat combining was escalating and grain dealers Friday said dry, warm weather should allow active harvesting this weekend across Oklahoma and southern Kansas.
The soft red winter harvest also was beginning in the southern portion of the U.S. growing region and there have been reports of better-than-expected yields there as well.
Signals the market was technically oversold underpinned prices. The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for the July closed at 22 percent. An RSI of 30 or less is viewed as an oversold market.
CBOT wheat futures closed unchanged to 2-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with July down 2-1/4 at $3.34-3/4 a bushel.
Cargill Inc sold 1.5 million bushels of July, and Smith Barney sold one million July as did Tenco Inc, traders said.
Refco Inc bought five million bushels of July and several other funds also bought the July, a move viewed by traders as short covering.
E.D. and F. Man International bull spread 1.5 million bushels of July/September at six to 6-1/2 cents per bushel, premium September, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 24,000 contracts, above the 20,251 traded Thursday.
In wheat options, Rand Financial sold 300 December $4.00 calls at 14 cents and Tenco Inc sold 200 July $3.40 puts at six cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 6,000 contracts, above the 4,180 traded Thursday.
